title: Somatic in the East, Psychological in the West?: Investigating Clinically-Grounded Cross-Cultural Depression Symptom Expression in LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs with Western or Eastern cultural personas to select depression symptoms and evaluating whether the models replicate clinically established patterns (Western populations reporting more psychological symptoms, Eastern populations reporting more somatic symptoms). An inverse attribution task was also used to ask models which culture is more likely to express specific symptoms.

Comparing the degree of cultural alignment in symptom selection and attribution when the models are prompted in English versus the local languages of the target Eastern cultures (Chinese, Japanese, and Hindi).
